Problem Statement¶

Context¶

AllLife Bank is a US bank that has a growing customer base. The majority of these customers are liability customers (depositors) with varying sizes of deposits. The number of customers who are also borrowers (asset customers) is quite small, and the bank is interested in expanding this base rapidly to bring in more loan business and in the process, earn more through the interest on loans. In particular, the management wants to explore ways of converting its liability customers to personal loan customers (while retaining them as depositors).

A campaign that the bank ran last year for liability customers showed a healthy conversion rate of over 9% success. This has encouraged the retail marketing department to devise campaigns with better target marketing to increase the success ratio.

You as a Data scientist at AllLife bank have to build a model that will help the marketing department to identify the potential customers who have a higher probability of purchasing the loan.

Objective¶

To predict whether a liability customer will buy personal loans, to understand which customer attributes are most significant in driving purchases, and identify which segment of customers to target more.

Data Dictionary¶

  • ID: Customer ID
  • Age: Customer’s age in completed years
  • Experience: #years of professional experience
  • Income: Annual income of the customer (in thousand dollars)
  • ZIP Code: Home Address ZIP code.
  • Family: the Family size of the customer
  • CCAvg: Average spending on credit cards per month (in thousand dollars)
  • Education: Education Level. 1: Undergrad; 2: Graduate;3: Advanced/Professional
  • Mortgage: Value of house mortgage if any. (in thousand dollars)
  • Personal_Loan: Did this customer accept the personal loan offered in the last campaign? (0: No, 1: Yes)
  • Securities_Account: Does the customer have securities account with the bank? (0: No, 1: Yes)
  • CD_Account: Does the customer have a certificate of deposit (CD) account with the bank? (0: No, 1: Yes)
  • Online: Do customers use internet banking facilities? (0: No, 1: Yes)
  • CreditCard: Does the customer use a credit card issued by any other Bank (excluding All life Bank)? (0: No, 1: Yes)

Exploratory Data Analysis.¶

  • EDA is an important part of any project involving data.
  • It is important to investigate and understand the data better before building a model with it.
  • A few questions have been mentioned below which will help you approach the analysis in the right manner and generate insights from the data.
  • A thorough analysis of the data, in addition to the questions mentioned below, should be done.

Questions:

  1. What is the distribution of mortgage attribute? Are there any noticeable patterns or outliers in the distribution?
  2. How many customers have credit cards?
  3. What are the attributes that have a strong correlation with the target attribute (personal loan)?
  4. How does a customer's interest in purchasing a loan vary with their age?
  5. How does a customer's interest in purchasing a loan vary with their education?

def detect_outliers_iqr(data, column):
    Q1 = data[column].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = data[column].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    outliers = data[(data[column] < lower) | (data[column] > upper)]
    print(f"{column}: {len(outliers)} outliers detected")
    return outliers

for col in ['Income', 'CCAvg', 'Mortgage']:
    detect_outliers_iqr(df, col)

CCAvg: 324 outliers detected
Mortgage: 291 outliers detected
In [35]:
def cap_outliers_iqr(df, column):
    """
        This function caps the outliers in a specified column of a DataFrame using the IQR method.
        It calculates the upper bound based on the IQR and clips values above this bound.
    """
    Q1 = df[column].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = df[column].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
    df[column] = df[column].clip(upper=upper_bound)
    print(f"{column} Capped values above {upper_bound:.2f}")
    return df

for col in ['Income', 'CCAvg', 'Mortgage']:
    df = cap_outliers_iqr(df, col)
    

Income Capped values above 186.50
CCAvg Capped values above 5.20
Mortgage Capped values above 252.50

Model Building¶

Model Evaluation Criterion¶

  • F1 Score: Harmonic mean of precision and recall, useful in our case where we want to optimize both false positives and false negatives.

Model Performance Improvement¶

For model performance improvement, we can consider the following techniques:

Pre Pruning¶

  • Setting the max_depth to prevent overfitting
  • Limiting the min_samples_leaf to avoid splits on very small samples
In [56]:
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
tuned_dt = DecisionTreeClassifier()
param_grid = {
    'max_depth': [i for i in range(1, 11)],
    'min_samples_leaf': [i for i in range(1, 21)],
}

grid_search = GridSearchCV(
    estimator=tuned_dt,
    param_grid=param_grid,
    scoring='f1',
    n_jobs=5,
    cv=5,
)

grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)

print("Best Parameters:", grid_search.best_params_)

Best Parameters: {'max_depth': 6, 'min_samples_leaf': 11}

models = []
for alpha in ccp_alphas:

We will select the post pruned model as it has better f1 score and accuracy as compared to the the other two models. The tuned model also has a better balance between precision and recall, making it more suitable for our use case where we want to minimize false positives and false negatives.

Actionable Insights and Business Recommendations¶

  • What recommedations would you suggest to the bank?

  1. Target High-Income Customers: Customers with higher annual incomes show a significantly greater likelihood of accepting personal loans. The bank should prioritize marketing campaigns towards this customer segment to maximize conversion rates.

  2. Focus on Customers with Higher Credit Card Spending (CCAvg): There is a strong positive correlation between average monthly credit card spending and personal loan acceptance. Customers with higher CCAvg are more likely to take personal loans, making them an attractive target group.

  3. Leverage Education Level: Customers with graduate or advanced/professional degrees have a much higher acceptance rate for personal loans compared to undergraduates. Tailoring loan products and marketing messages to appeal to these education segments can improve campaign effectiveness.

  4. Consider Mortgage Holders: Loan acceptance rates increase with higher mortgage amounts. Customers with substantial mortgages may have greater financial needs and can be targeted for cross-selling personal loans.

  5. Balanced Approach to Credit Card Holders: Since credit card ownership does not significantly influence loan acceptance, campaigns should not exclude non-credit card holders.

  6. Personalized Offers: Use the predictive model to score existing liability customers and identify those with the highest probability of accepting a loan. Personalized offers can then be sent to these high-propensity customers.

By implementing these recommendations, AllLife Bank can improve the efficiency of its marketing campaigns, increase personal loan uptake, and drive higher revenue from its existing customer base.
